limitations: ApoMarioHighscore and recordRunEnd are requested future APIs and are not present in the repository, outline, or code-model; their exact implementation anchors cannot be inspected.
No test sources or build configuration for the requested feature were inspected.
The source does not define a dedicated human-name input or clarify multi-player highscore inclusion policy.
The existing elapsed-time helper depends on randomLevel; the inspected code does not establish that it is non-null for every editor or externally loaded level.

nodes.label: Completed-run highscore record: score, player name, survival time
Player identity shown in highscore and analysis views
Persisted highscore file and ordered board
Menu and analysis presentation of run results
User-edited highscore store to highscore parser and menu
nodes.sink: The proposed ApoMarioHighscore load/parser, in-memory record lists, sorting, and the dedicated menu highscore panel.
nodes.source: The feature's local highscore store file; existing local persistence uses file streams in ApoMarioConstants#loadProperties() and #saveProperties().
nodes.untrusted_input: Bytes, records, names, scores, and times in the Path supplied to ApoMarioHighscore(java.nio.file.Path) can be edited by the local user.

nodes.label: Mutable run state to run-end recording
nodes.source: ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis(boolean) reads and updates ApoMarioPlayer points; ApoMarioLevel#getTime()/#getPassedTime() expose timer state; analysis derives names from human/AI state.
nodes.untrusted_input: In-game score, timer, visibility, AI identity, and player fields can be locally tampered with before run completion.

nodes.label: Shared/local level content to level decoder and run state
nodes.sink: ApoMarioLevel allocations, entity construction, player/finish placement, and ultimately score/time state used at run end.
nodes.source: ApoMarioLevelIO#readLevel(DataInputStream), reached through ApoIO#readLevel(boolean,String); the latter supports local files and URL streams.
nodes.untrusted_input: Binary level dimensions, tile values, enemy counts, coordinates, and timer values from a user-edited file or shared level server.

nodes.label: User-selected AI class/file to player identity and highscore name
nodes.sink: Dynamic class loading, ApoMarioPlayer AI/team-name state, analysis name derivation, and the proposed highscore record.
nodes.source: ApoMarioLevel#loadPlayer(int,String) and ApoMarioClassLoader#loadClassData(String) read user-selected AI artifacts.
nodes.untrusted_input: A local user-selected class path and class bytes can determine an AI's team name and author, which can then be used as the displayed/player name.

nodes.label: Run completion is handled by ApoMarioLevel#setAnalysis(boolean), which computes bonus points, mutates player points, sets the component win flag, and switches to the analysis panel.
nodes.task_relevance: This is the integration point where the completed run's final score should be captured.
nodes.verification: Trace both win and loss calls to setAnalysis(boolean) and confirm recording occurs after the final point mutation and before panel transition.

nodes.label: ApoMarioPlayer stores points and exposes getPoints(); ApoMarioLevel#getTime() exposes the remaining timer, while getPassedTime() computes elapsed time as randomLevel.getTime() minus the remaining time.
nodes.task_relevance: The feature must select the actual final score and elapsed duration, not a display-only or reset value.
nodes.verification: Exercise a win and loss and compare recorded values with the final player points and timer delta before restart.

nodes.label: The analysis view derives a human name as "human" and an AI name from the AI team name and player number; ApoMarioPlayer#setAi also copies AI team name and author into player state.
nodes.task_relevance: The run-end integration must use the intended player identity and must not accept an absent/null name as a valid display identity.
nodes.verification: Run with a human player and an AI player and compare the name passed to recording with the analysis display name.

nodes.label: The menu currently has no highscore panel or highscore action; its visible buttons are configured through BUTTON_MENU and its render method draws player statistics and menu controls.
nodes.task_relevance: The requested dedicated highscore view requires new panel state, navigation, rendering, and button wiring.
nodes.verification: Inspect menu navigation and BUTTON_MENU after implementation; select the highscore action and verify the dedicated panel is rendered.

nodes.label: The existing properties loader catches I/O errors, prints a message, then continues with defaults; several numeric properties are parsed and bounded, but this behavior is not an implementation of highscore record validation.
nodes.task_relevance: It provides a persistence pattern but does not establish safe parsing for the new record format.
nodes.verification: Review the new highscore parser independently; do not infer its validation behavior from properties loading.

nodes.label: The binary level reader takes width and height from input, allocates a two-dimensional entity array, and iterates input-controlled dimensions and enemy counts while constructing entities.
nodes.task_relevance: A highscore implementation must avoid copying this unbounded allocation/loop pattern when reading its store.
nodes.verification: Test malformed dimensions/counts and observe allocation and loop limits; use this as a regression check for the highscore parser.

nodes.failure_behavior: Existing behavior is not changed by this context; the new highscore path must reject oversized records before allocation and report the rejection.
nodes.label: The existing binary level reader allocates and loops using dimensions/counts read from untrusted level data without an evident explicit upper-bound check in the shown operation, making resource exhaustion reachable from a malformed local or shared level.
nodes.task_relevance: The new feature consumes level-derived values and should not add another unbounded parser or rely on unsafe decoded state.
nodes.verification: Supply oversized width/height/count values through a test level and verify the decoder rejects them before allocation.

nodes.failure_behavior: The store operation rejects malformed, out-of-range, or structurally inconsistent records and reports rejection; the panel falls back to an empty valid board so menu display still occurs.
nodes.label: A user-edited highscore file could tamper with scores, names, ordering fields, or survival times, causing the board to display false performance or a forged player identity if records are trusted after parsing.
nodes.task_relevance: The requested persistent board is a direct sink for local file tampering.
nodes.verification: Create malformed and deliberately reordered store files; verify invalid records are reported/rejected, valid records remain point-descending, and the menu still opens with an empty or valid board.

nodes.failure_behavior: The parser rejects oversized counts, names, and numeric ranges and reports rejection; the caller uses a bounded empty/default board and continues menu initialization.
nodes.label: A malformed highscore file with huge counts, names, or numeric values could cause excessive allocation, long parsing, integer overflow, or UI disruption before the board is displayed.
nodes.task_relevance: The required public list accessors make parser-created collections and strings part of the feature's attack surface.
nodes.verification: Fuzz/truncate the store and test maximum-plus-one counts, name lengths, scores, and times; assert bounded memory/time and a reported rejection.

nodes.failure_behavior: At the completion integration point, normalize missing/invalid run values to stated safe defaults and invoke recording once after final score calculation; do not skip the primary record effect.
nodes.label: If recording is attached before the final scoring mutations or to only one terminal path, the board can store an intermediate score or omit a loss/clear run.
nodes.task_relevance: The task explicitly requires recording on both clearing a level and losing with the real final values.
nodes.verification: Test clear, timer expiry, falling death, and AI exception paths; assert exactly one record per finished run and that it contains post-scoring values.

nodes.failure_behavior: The integration normalizes a missing/invalid name to a bounded default before storeRun; storeRun rejects invalid names and reports rejection, while the caller still records using the default.
nodes.label: If AI team names or local class artifacts are copied into highscore display without length and character validation, a user can spoof identity or create oversized/unexpected displayed text.
nodes.task_relevance: The feature persists and displays the player's name, including names derived from AI state.
nodes.verification: Use null, empty, overlong, control-character, and AI-derived names and verify normalization/rejection and bounded rendering.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject and report any malformed tuple, mismatched list cardinality, or invalid numeric value; the menu caller uses an empty valid board as the stated default so the highscore view still renders.
nodes.label: The ApoMarioHighscore store/load operation must preserve each valid record as a synchronized name-score-survival-time tuple and must return all three lists in the same point-descending order; it must not trust a file-provided ordering field.
nodes.task_relevance: The task requires persisted names sorted by points descending and exposes parallel public lists.
nodes.verification: Persist multiple records with shuffled input order and equal/negative/overflowing values; reload and assert synchronized lists sorted by descending score, with invalid input rejected.

nodes.failure_behavior: storeRun rejects and reports invalid input without substituting/clamping; setAnalysis/recordRunEnd normalizes absent or invalid score, elapsed time, and name to documented defaults before invoking storeRun.
nodes.label: The storeRun(int,String,int) operation must validate score, survivalTime, and playerName as one record and the integration must normalize missing or invalid run values to explicit defaults before calling it, so a finished run is still recorded.
nodes.task_relevance: The task requires real score, player name, and mm:ss survival time at run end.
nodes.verification: Unit-test storeRun with null, blank, overlong, invalid-character, negative, and overflow values; integration-test a normal run and verify the normalized fallback is passed rather than skipping recording.

nodes.failure_behavior: Reject and report oversized, truncated, or otherwise invalid input before allocation; if persistence fails, retain the in-memory valid board and report the write failure, while the caller continues displaying the board.
nodes.label: The highscore parser and persistAcrossRuns operation must impose bounded file size, record count, name length, and numeric ranges before allocating strings/lists or sorting, and must use safe replacement or atomic write semantics for persistence.
nodes.task_relevance: The board is persisted in a local user-editable file and its public list accessors expose parser allocations.
nodes.verification: Test empty, truncated, oversized, and unwritable stores; verify bounded resource use, explicit rejection/reporting, and that a failed write does not erase the in-memory valid records.

nodes.failure_behavior: If level state is missing or invalid, normalize to documented defaults and still call the primary record operation; do not silently suppress recording. Prevent duplicate calls with an explicit terminal-state guard.
nodes.label: The completion integration must invoke recordRunEnd exactly once for every real one-player run ending in a level clear or loss, after final score mutation and before the level is restarted or replaced; replay, simulation, and editor-only runs must be explicitly excluded or separately identified.
nodes.task_relevance: The task requires the running game itself to record each finished run's actual values.
nodes.verification: Instrument recordRunEnd and cover clear, loss, timer expiry, restart, replay, simulation, editor, and repeated terminal callbacks; assert the intended once-per-run matrix.

nodes.failure_behavior: storeRun rejects invalid names and reports rejection; recordRunEnd normalizes them to the stated default before calling storeRun so the run is still recorded and displayed.
nodes.label: The player-name derivation and storeRun operation must accept only a bounded, display-safe canonical name; the integration must convert null/blank/invalid human or AI names to a documented default before calling storeRun.
nodes.task_relevance: The feature must persist and display the player's name while local AI artifacts and team names are user-controlled.
nodes.verification: Test human, AI, null, blank, control-character, delimiter, and overlong names through the integration and direct storeRun API.

nodes.failure_behavior: On load rejection, report the error and use an empty valid board; continue initializing and make the dedicated view navigable.
nodes.label: The menu integration must load the persisted board during panel initialization, expose a dedicated highscore view/action, and render names, descending scores, and survival times as mm:ss without allowing malformed store text to reach rendering.
nodes.task_relevance: The task requires a dedicated menu panel/view and persistence across application runs.
nodes.verification: Start a fresh process with valid records, malformed records, and no store; verify persistence, sorting, mm:ss formatting, dedicated navigation, and safe fallback rendering.

nodes.label: Verify R1 by round-tripping valid and malformed tuple files and asserting equal list lengths, synchronized indexes, and descending score order.
nodes.task_relevance: Checks persisted board integrity and sorting.
nodes.verification: Automated round-trip and malformed-input tests.

nodes.label: Verify R2 and R5 with direct API boundary tests and integration tests for normalization, rejection, and continued recording.
nodes.task_relevance: Checks input validation for score, elapsed time, and name.
nodes.verification: Boundary and integration tests for invalid values and names.

nodes.label: Verify R3 with fuzzed/truncated/oversized stores and simulated write failures, checking rejection reporting, bounded resource use, and retention of the in-memory valid board.
nodes.task_relevance: Checks persistence resilience and denial-of-service resistance.
nodes.verification: Resource-bound and failure-injection tests.

nodes.label: Verify R4 by instrumenting the terminal callback across clear, loss, timer, restart, replay, simulation, and editor flows and asserting exactly one intended record per real run.
nodes.task_relevance: Checks complete-run coverage and duplicate prevention.
nodes.verification: Terminal-path integration test matrix.

nodes.label: Verify R6 by launching with valid, invalid, missing, and previously persisted stores and checking dedicated view navigation, names, descending points, and mm:ss output.
nodes.task_relevance: Checks the user-visible menu feature and fallback behavior.
nodes.verification: End-to-end menu/persistence tests.

nodes.failure_behavior: Until resolved, use an explicit bounded default name and a deterministic application-local store path at the integration point.
nodes.label: The supplied source and outline do not establish a user-editable player-name input field or a canonical configured Path for the future highscore store; implementation must choose and document the source/default for a human name and store location.
nodes.task_relevance: These choices affect authenticity, persistence scope, and test setup.
nodes.verification: Review the implemented constructor call and human-name source against the product requirement and public API tests.

nodes.failure_behavior: Until resolved, apply the task's single running-player interpretation and document the selected player index; do not silently record multiple ambiguous tuples.
nodes.label: The inspected code does not establish whether recordRunEnd should include only the human player, the winning player in two-player mode, or every visible player; setAnalysis(boolean) contains distinct one-player and two-player scoring branches.
nodes.task_relevance: The choice changes which score/name/time tuple is written and whether AI or opponent runs enter the board.
nodes.verification: Exercise one- and two-player runs and compare the recorded tuple count/player selection with the documented policy.

nodes.failure_behavior: Until resolved, retain the original file, report rejection, and use an empty in-memory board without destructive deletion.
nodes.label: The inspected code does not establish whether a malformed existing highscore store should be quarantined, deleted, or retained alongside a replacement file; current properties loading only reports an I/O exception and continues.
nodes.task_relevance: This affects recovery and preservation of user data when persistence is first introduced.
nodes.verification: Inject malformed stores and inspect whether the implementation preserves the original bytes while continuing with the stated fallback.

summary: The feature will consume mutable run state, derive a player identity and elapsed time, write/read a local highscore store, and display ordered records from a menu panel. Existing completion, score, time, player-name derivation, menu-panel switching, and file-loading paths are anchored below; the highscore type itself is not present in the repository model.
